Round 12 · The rebuild, measured against the real thing

Look first. Measure second.

The method changed: the round opens by looking at ours beside the arcade and by an agent playing it, not by measuring constants to four decimals. R12 shipped two whole missing systems — land under stage 1 and real stakes (a game-over) — plus roll-drama, a visible tracer, and gun fire that now lands at the sight. It holds at 8.0: more After Burner than before, but the missile is reachable and still not usable, and the sky still goes quiet.
“More After Burner than R11 — carrier launch, a swinging horizon, islands, a visible tracer, gun kills at the sight, a real game-over — but I still can’t use my missiles, planes still die on my wingtip, and the sky still goes dead.”
R12 fresh-context judge · composite 8.0 (motion 7.5 · stills 8.5)

Ours vs the arcade

stage 1 · 60 Hz capture vs mapped longplay

Shipped this round

held up under the judge’s re-measure
  • Missile LOCK is reachable — the geometry bug is fixed (band was above the sight’s cone)
  • Gun kills resolve at the sight (p90 14.6 → ~10 %W), not at the wingtip
  • Tracer is a visible bright column, not a few faint dots
  • Stage 1 has islands, crags and surf; cloud banks grew
  • Real stakes — a proper GAME OVER instead of a silent life refill
  • Attract mode banks hard (horizon swings ±60°) instead of cruising level

Next — R13

ranked by what breaks the illusion
  1. 01 FEEL
    Missiles are reachable but not usable

    The lock can form now, but only by climbing to the horizon band and sitting there — which gets you shot. The judge got one lock in 45 turns and never fired a salvo in real play. Route enemies through the lock band (or widen the strip) so a lock happens from normal posture — not a wider sight.

  2. 02 FEEL
    Kills still happen to you — no gunnery window

    The gun now kills at the sight, but enemies pop from horizon-dot to wingtip with no stretch at a shootable mid-range depth. Give enemies time at a depth the player can actually aim at.

  3. 03 MISSING
    The sky still goes dead

    Confirmed multi-second stretches with zero enemies, and no large-scale flyby — an enemy crossing the screen at size, the way the arcade’s do every second or two. Population and choreography, not size.

  4. 04 FEEL
    The jet doesn’t breathe fire

    The arcade trails big orange afterburner cones — the game’s name. Ours has black nozzle rings with small dots. Carried from the gestalt pass.

  5. 05 POLISH
    Climaxes and the title

    Kill fireballs read small next to the arcade’s half-screen blasts; the title wordmark is hand-rounded where the arcade’s is brush-angular. Lower priority than the combat feel.

Keep — do not regress

  • Missile lock + salvo mechanism works (don’t regress the geometry fix)
  • Gun kills at the sight; blind-pilot gain is protected
  • Islands, the game-over path, and the ±60° attract drama
  • Death starburst → tumble → READY; stage 2 sunset composition

R12 was the method’s first full turn: look first, play it (an agent, no human waited on), ship missing systems before tuning constants, and let the judge re-measure every claim — which caught the missile being reachable-not-usable and an over-stated TL commit. Full history in judging/R12/.
